summary: Cupica Airport (BHF) is a small regional airfield serving Bahía Solano on Colombia's remote Pacific coast in the Chocó department, one of the wettest and most biodiverse regions on the planet. It functions as the primary air gateway for travelers heading to Bahía Solano, El Valle, and nearby Ensenada de Utría National Park. The airport handles short-haul flights mainly from Medellín and is essential for connecting this otherwise hard-to-reach coastal area to the rest of Colombia.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Cupica Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by small regional carriers such as SATENA and ADA, with scheduled flights connecting Bahía Solano to Medellín and occasionally other Colombian cities.

Q: How far is the airport from Bahía Solano town center?
A: Cupica Airport is located only a few kilometers from Bahía Solano's town center, typically a short 10–15 minute taxi or mototaxi ride.

Q: When is the best time to visit this region?
A: The dry season between June and September offers the best weather and coincides with humpback whale watching season, when these magnificent creatures migrate to nearby waters to breed.

Q: Are there ATMs or banking services at the airport?
A: No, the airport has very limited facilities. Travelers should bring cash in Colombian pesos from larger cities, as banking services in Bahía Solano itself are also scarce.
transport_tips: Taxis and mototaxis are the main options for getting between the airport and Bahía Solano or El Valle; rides should be arranged in advance as services are informal. Road travel in the region can be slow and affected by heavy rainfall, so flying remains the most reliable way in and out. Pack light and be prepared for luggage weight limits typical of small aircraft operating in remote areas.
